name: Ingrid Kaur
life: “I still remember washing paint off my grandson's hands over a bucket.” Thursday often includes a stop at the corner outside Coastal Barber, where Ingrid usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
voice: I can fit a sink if the room is used after school one evening a week. My grandson needs someplace to wash his brushes.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a plum-colored cardigan and a watch on a cracked leather band. Ingrid has a crooked front tooth visible when laughing, with silver temples and a dark fringe. Ingrid presses the lips together to keep a smile in during a conversation.
personality: Ingrid treats keeping somebody waiting as a serious discourtesy. This can turn a helpful person into an impatient one when everybody else needs a slower conversation.
agenda: To fit a wash basin and open one session to children.
family: Ren Trent is Ingrid’s younger relative by marriage. A relative left a box of miscellaneous screws beside a perfectly labeled set of good tools. The box was the first thing the family fought over after the funeral. Ingrid tries to repair an ordinary thing before offering to buy a new one. Asked about *The empty drum stool*, Ren says, “I kept the invitation because I want to offer my chair at the orchestra rehearsal the same way.”
connections: Emma Davis. A free sitting for a pensioner and an after-school session share the same sink.
